_comment: Configuration for the Farm Water Analysis dashboard generator (lib/build_dashboard.py). Edit these values as the garden / irrigation plan changes; no code changes needed.

bed._comment: Physical geometry of the metered tomato raised bed, recorded 2026-08-03. This is the missing conversion that makes metered litres interpretable as inches of water. Everything metered by the WFC01 lands on THIS bed only; peppers are a separate unmetered line.

target._comment: target_in_per_week is Justin's stated goal. NOTE it is a classic in-ground, moderate-weather rule of thumb; a 10-inch-deep raised bed in a Santa Clara August loses considerably more. august_etc_in_per_week is the estimated real crop demand (reference ET0 ~0.25-0.35 in/day x tomato mid-season Kc ~1.15). Water to the ETc figure in a heat event and drift back toward target_in_per_week in Sept/Oct.

storage._comment: Plant-available water held by the whole 10-inch profile at an assumed AWC of 0.12-0.20 in per inch of soil. The point: a single 129 L dose is ~1.14 in, i.e. it tries to deliver most of the profile's ENTIRE available capacity in one 12-minute shot. That is why it drains.

emitters._comment: Audited 2026-08-03 against the measured 12.4 L/min line flow. Bubblers are adjustable 0-13 gph; back-solving from the meter puts them at ~13.4 gph each, i.e. WIDE OPEN, at or past spec. Do not throttle them far below ~half — the 8-stream full-circle pattern needs flow to distribute evenly, and a starved bubbler dribbles out one side. Use WFC01 cycle mode, not the bubbler threads, as the primary volume/rate control.

drip_flags.note: fixed rate; alone this is a 1.20 in/hr floor

infiltration._comment: The core problem found 2026-08-03. Instantaneous application rate is several times what the soil can absorb, so past the first minute or two water ponds, runs to the edges and channels down preferential paths instead of wetting the profile evenly. Effective (duty-cycled) rate should sit at or under the ceiling.

health._comment: Sensor-trust thresholds. nominal_volts is the voltage the probe's factory calibration assumes (1.5 V alkaline); a lithium AA reads ~1.7 V and shifts the derived moisture %. range_collapse_frac flags a probe whose daily AD swing drops below this fraction of its trailing norm (failing sensor or lost soil contact).

plan._comment: Actual watering is a fixed timer, not a volume-based/Smart plan (that was never implemented). The WFC01 meters the tomato raised bed line ONLY; peppers run on a separate, unmetered timer. Delivery figures below are the MEASURED metered rate on clean days, not a nameplate estimate — real flow runs well above emitter nameplate.

schedule_log.change: Tomato timer set: 14 min once daily @ 05:05 PT (fixed-timer, replacing earlier irregular hand-timing).
Tomato timer trimmed 14 → 10 min to cut leaching / deep percolation; watch the overnight probe min holds near 58–60% at 3 in.
Pepper bags moved from every-12 h to once daily, 15 min @ 06:45 PT; watch the 2-in probe for a deeper daily dry-down (bag bottoms may still stay wet).

DECISION: hold peppers at once daily 15 min through the week of Jul 27 despite an apparent net daily deficit (AD baseline −3 to −4 counts/day vs only +2 recovery per dose). Pepper probe is on a lithium battery (1.70 V vs 1.50 V nominal) since Jul 18, so its % scale is shifted and its AD range has collapsed — deficit reading is unconfirmed. Escalation tripwires handed to on-site helper; re-evaluate on the Aug 1 site visit.

10-min run confirmed at 118 L/day measured over the 9 clean 10-min days Jul 24–Aug 1, vs 168.6 L/day at 14 min — ratio 0.70 against the theoretical 0.714. metered_daily/metered_weekly are now MEASURED 10-min figures (118 / 825, the latter an actual observed Jul 26–Aug 1 seven-day total, not an extrapolation) and the old 14-min estimate note is retired. The back-filled Jul 26 export resolved what looked like a 229.8 L spike on Jul 27 into two normal days (123.6 / 106.2).

Tomato timer raised 10 → 12 min once daily @ 05:05 PT, effective the Aug 3 run. Rationale: at 10 min the tomato daily mean fell steadily 64.6 → 60.5 over Jul 26–Aug 1 (−0.68 pts/day, ≈ −4.8 %/wk vs the −0.6 %/wk 34-day regression) and the overnight min broke below the 58–60% watch band to 53 — the trim over-corrected for current ET. Expect metered draw to rise to roughly 142 L/day / ~990 L/wk (118 × 12/10); re-measure and update metered_daily/metered_weekly from clean days once the next exports land. Watch that the overnight min recovers back into 58–60%.

DECISION: keep the tomato start at 05:05 PT rather than moving it toward sunrise (06:13 on Aug 2, drifting to 06:25 by Aug 16). Original motive for the early slot — avoiding overlap with the property's other zone timers — holds up. Rationale: (a) the water-at-sunrise rule is a foliar-disease argument and does not apply to soil-level bubblers/drip-flag emitters; (b) measured overnight loss is ~0.13 pts/hr (60.4 @18:00 → 59.0 @05:00) vs ~1.1 pts/hr daytime (71.7 @08:00 → 60.4 @18:00), so pre-dawn application costs ~nothing evaporatively; (c) infiltration lag already lands the recharge where you'd want it — the 3-in probe first registers the pulse ~06:00 and peaks 08:00, about 2 h AFTER sunrise, so a later start would only push peak deeper into the demand curve; (d) control here is timer-based, and daily draw already varies 106–128 L (CV 5.5%, implied flow 10.6–12.8 L/min), so moving into the shared-pressure window would add flow variance to the one variable being calibrated by minutes. Also avoids confounding the 10→12 min change taking effect Aug 3.

NEXT LEVER if 12 min fails to lift the overnight min back into 58–60%: split the dose rather than adjusting time-of-day or adding more minutes to a single run. The 07:00–11:00 plateau at 70–71% reads as the bed sitting at field capacity and shedding the excess, which is a percolation loss that a longer single run would worsen. Try ~7 min @ 05:05 + ~7 min mid-afternoon at similar total volume; this also stays clear of the other zones' morning window.

BED GEOMETRY RECORDED (12 x 4 ft, 48 sq ft, soil 10 in deep) and it overturns the prior read of this system. 1 inch of water over the bed = 113.3 L. Current delivery of ~124-129 L/day is therefore ~1.1 in/DAY = ~7.7-8.0 in/WEEK, against a stated target of 1.0-1.5 in/week — roughly 6x over. A single dose is ~1.14 in, close to the entire plant-available capacity of the 10-inch profile (1.2-2.0 in), delivered in 12 minutes. The bed has never been under-watered; it has been flood-dosed daily, which is why the probe spikes to 90%+ and sheds 15 points in 45 minutes.

ROOT CAUSE: application RATE, not duration or timing. Measured line flow 12.4 L/min over 48 sq ft = 6.6 in/hr instantaneous, vs 0.2-0.6 in/hr for loam and maybe 1-3 in/hr for a loose raised-bed mix. Past the first minute or two water ponds, runs to the edges and channels rather than wetting the profile. Emitter audit: 9 drip flags @4 gph = 136 L/h fixed (a 1.20 in/hr floor on their own), leaving the 12 adjustable bubblers at ~13.4 gph each — wide open, at or past their 13 gph spec.

SUPERSEDES the Aug 2 'next lever' entry (7 min AM + 7 min PM). That was written without bed area and would have delivered ~174 L/day = 10.7 in/week — worse than the problem it was meant to fix. Ignore it.

NEW PLAN (WFC01 cycle mode as the primary rate control, NOT the bubbler threads — an 8-stream full-circle bubbler throttled too far loses its pattern and dribbles out one side). Cycle 30 s ON / 90 s OFF = 25% duty = 1.65 in/hr effective, which sits inside the raised-bed infiltration window. Run ~6 min elapsed (~1.5 min of actual flow, ~18.6 L) twice daily at 05:05 and ~17:30 => ~37 L/day = 0.33 in/day = 2.30 in/week. That targets estimated August ETc (1.75-2.45 in/wk), not the 1.0-1.5 in/wk shoulder-season figure. Step down over ~5 days rather than cutting from 129 L in one go, and watch the overnight min. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION: if the rate diagnosis is right, retained soil moisture should RISE while total volume FALLS, because a larger share of a smaller dose actually infiltrates. If the overnight min keeps dropping as volume comes down, the diagnosis is wrong and the deficit is real.

OPEN ITEM: the dashboard's irrigation panel narrative is now stale — it still hardcodes the 14-min run, the ~820 L expectation, and the claim that 'there is no volume target'. With bed geometry recorded there IS a volume target (113 L per inch). Needs a template pass.

Pepper probe battery swap (lithium 1.70 V → alkaline 1.50 V) scheduled for later the week of Aug 3. Pepper moisture is NOT trustworthy until then: AD range has collapsed to 4–6 counts (was 50–89 before Jul 22) with daily min/max nearly identical, i.e. no diurnal signal at all, so the apparent Jul 27–Aug 1 decline (43.8 → 40.5) reads as calibration drift rather than a real dry-down. After the swap, confirm the AD range recovers before acting on any pepper number.
